The only genuinely adverse signals are that the device 'Trident/7.0 | Windows 10 | ie 11.0 for desktop | 1920x1080' is New for this account and product 'R' never appears in the 82-transaction baseline; online is only 4.9% of history. There is no burst (one online txn in the episode), no card-testing run, no proxy, no rare shared device and no linked cards, so patterns 1, 3, 4 and the coordinated/undocumented bucket are not supported. Two prior confirmed account-takeover cases on this same card (CC-2277, CC-2447, Aug 2016, $81.93 and $33.95) are real context and keep this above a routine clear, but those were small mixed-channel items reported by the cardholder, and nothing here replicates that signature. Under R1/pattern-2 guidance a single unusual online purchase at probability well under 0.70 is ambiguous, so the correct step is verification; semantic memory (CC-5236, CC-0099, CC-5224) shows this shape usually resolves as a legitimate purchase from a new device.
